stem:
Which one of the following is the correct set up to determine the melting point of ice?

(The figure shows four set-ups with a thermometer on a stand. (I) a beaker of 'Ice + salt' with the thermometer bulb in it. (II) a beaker of 'Ice' (block ice) with the thermometer. (III) a beaker of 'Crushed ice' with the thermometer held vertically, bulb immersed in the crushed ice. (IV) a beaker of 'Crushed ice' with the thermometer clamped at a slant/tilted angle.)

A glass tumbler containing hot water is kept in the freezer compartment of a refrigerator. If you could measure the temperature of the content of the tumbler, which of the following graph would correctly represent the change in its temperature as a function of time?

(The figure shows four Temperature-vs-Time graphs with \(0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\) marked. (I) temperature falls, plateaus at \(0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\), then falls further below \(0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\). (II) temperature falls steadily in a straight line with no plateau. (III) temperature falls and stays flat at \(0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\). (IV) temperature falls then rises again.)

stem:
Ram heats a beaker containing ice and water. He measures the temperature of the content of the beaker as a function of time. Which of the following would correctly represent the result?

(The figure shows four Temperature-vs-Time graphs with \(0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\) and \(100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\) marked. (I) starts near \(0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\), rises steeply to \(100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\) then plateaus at \(100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\). (II) starts at \(100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\) and falls to \(0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\). (III) starts at \(100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\), plateaus, then falls to \(0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\). (IV) starts at \(0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\), holds a plateau at \(0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\), then rises toward \(100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\).)

stem:
The temperature-time graph given alongside shows the heating curve for pure wax. What is the boiling point of the substance?

(The figure plots Temperature (\(^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\), with \(15\) and \(110\) marked) against Time. The curve rises to \(15^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\) (points A-A1), holds a flat plateau at \(15^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\) (A1-B-B1), rises through C to \(110^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\) (B1-D1), then holds a flat plateau at \(110^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\) (D1-D-D2).)
